newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Blast reported in Damascus bus station.
newsitem.headline: Blast reported in Damascus bus station.

text.p: An explosion rocked a bus station in the Syrian capital Damascus on Tuesday, destroying a bus and causing casualties, a resident diplomat said on Thursday.

The diplomat said large numbers of police sealed off the area after the explosion in the Baramkeh district and streets were blocked with traffic trying to flee. A traveller who was in Damascus on Tuesday said the blast was caused by a bomb, which killed about 15 people.

"A bomb placed in a bag exploded in the luggage compartment of a bus at Al-Intilak Centre, the main taxi and bus stop in Damascus. The bus belonged to Trans Tours company and was heading to Aleppo (in northern Syria)," the traveller said.
"At least 15 people were killed and 50 wounded in the blast."

The diplomat, speaking by telephone, stressed that reliable information was very difficult to obtain and that on Thursday there was no sign of any incident at the bus station which lies close to the international fair and serves the route to Lebanon.
But he said other residents had quoted police as confirming there had been an explosion without giving further details.

Residents in Damascus said it was not clear who might have caused the blast. They noted that some incidents earlier in 1996 had been blamed on elements in Turkey while others recalled that there had been one or two attacks on Syrian targets in neighbouring Lebanon earlier in December.
Leaflets distributed in Beirut last month condemned Syria's military presence in Lebanon and criticised Lebanon's pro-Syrian government.
